source_text: An illud quidem iustum est, quod ipse facit, id est aliena peccata aliis imputando, et nobis praecipit, quod iniustum est, ut unumquemque pro voluntatis suae delictis reum pronuntiemus?
pass_a_gloss: Or is that indeed just which he himself does, that is by imputing others' sins to others, and does he precept to us what is unjust, that we pronounce each one a defendant for the offenses of his own will?

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will

pass_b_english: Or is what he does just—namely, charging some people with other people’s sins—while what he commands us to do is unjust: declaring each person guilty for the offenses of that person’s own will?

choices.why: Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: Continues the explicit argument from the law forbidding punishment of parents and children for one another’s sins.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
